stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Harness changes for banking-finance/compare-closing-documents-against-restructuring-conditions (INV dimension only). The base run (base1.md) completed the task successfully; every change below targets how it got there, not what it concluded.

1. NEW scripts/extract_all_docs.py — bulk document extraction with per-file sanity gates.
Moment: rollout lines 39–88. The runtime's scripts/read_doc.py failed under its sandbox default (FileNotFoundError: podman), and because the agent's loop ran with 2>&1, all nine "extracted" .txt files were 18-line Python tracebacks sitting where document text was expected — the run survived only because it sampled one file. It then had to read read_doc.py's own source (line 90) mid-task to discover --in host. The script drives read_doc.py --in host over documents/, writes .scratch/<name>.txt, prints a file-to-line-count inventory, and fails loudly per file (writes nothing for it, exits 1) if extraction errors, times out, returns a traceback, or yields under 20 non-empty lines; exits 2 with a bounded fallback message if read_doc.py is absent. Verified: py_compile; missing-reader path (exit 2); stub test exercising the traceback gate, tiny-output gate, and OK passthrough (failed files not written, exit 1).

2. tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md (was empty) — three tool facts, each anchored to a moment.
Lines 37–38: a /tmp scratch write was blocked by the external-directory permission rule — keep intermediates in .scratch/. Lines 39–90: the --in host fact plus one bounded fallback (if a file keeps failing, consume that document with the read tool and stop retrying the command). Line 2208: the read tool truncates at ~50 KB per call while the extracted corpus here is ~4,300 lines — continue long files with offset and use grep over .scratch/ text to verify quotes before citing them.

3. LongTermMEMORY.md (was empty) — workspace facts verified against this workspace's source files.
Lines 20–28 and 216: the nine-document inventory and roles — rsa-and-term-sheet.docx (RSA dated April 28, 2025 with the Term Sheet at Exhibit A) is the controlling benchmark; the other eight are the closing documents. Plus a fact base1 itself relied on: new-tl-credit-agreement.docx and es-asset-purchase-agreement.docx are expressly excerpted (bracketed omission notes verified in the source docx XML; mirrored in base1's own "not verifiable" report section). Recording it stops a future run from hunting for omitted sections or counting them as breaches. This is a file-status fact about this workspace, not a review rule.

4. guardrails.md (was empty) — two rules drawn from the run's two compactions.
Moments: lines 2194–2270 and 4654–4779 (two context compactions in one run) with the deliverable materializing only at the single ~46-KB write of line 5448. Every finding lived in conversation until that moment; a third compaction or one failed final write would have lost the run's work. Rule 1: persist findings to a scratch markdown file as each document is read (discrepancy, document, pinpoint section, quote). Rule 2: after a compaction, keep the deliverable advancing on disk — convert materially complete content into its final named file and re-extract it to confirm it parses before stopping. Two guardrail bullets rather than a skill because the failure mode is silent: nothing in the conversation would trigger a skill at the right moment.

Deliberately unchanged: systemprompt.md, skills/, plugin/, sub_agents/. The run got the method right — RSA first, benchmark checklist, per-document comparison, grep-verified quotes, the runtime docx skill for output, artifact validation before stopping (lines 5448–5520) — so no review-method skill is warranted and no skill-trigger lines are needed; no plugin (no repeatedly ignored prose to relocate); no subagent (the cross-document comparison needs all documents in one context; the 50-KB read cap is addressed by the extraction script instead).

Validation: py_compile passes; no template braces in any always-on file (systemprompt.md, guardrails.md, LongTermMEMORY.md, tool_guidance.md all grep-clean); the only script named in always-on text — extract_all_docs.py — ships in this proposal (read_doc.py is runtime-provided); stub-test artifacts removed; context/harness is 9 files.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
Harness edits — 2 changes. Dimension: practitioner knowledge (banking/finance review deliverables). All other files KEEP_BASE.

1. NEW SKILL skills/cite-check/SKILL.md — the pre-delivery cite-check pass a practitioner runs on any review deliverable: (i) recount every self-stated total and severity distribution from the artifact's own enumerated findings, under a stated counting convention; (ii) resolve every internal cross-reference ("see Item N") to the item that actually bears the point; (iii) re-verify every section citation and quotation against the cited source document immediately before delivery; re-run all three after any fix. Anchored with this workspace's base-run facts as evidence, labelled as such.

Trajectory moments — the base run's substantive analysis verified accurate against the sources, but the shipped artifact carried three defects no pass caught:
- base1.md:5506 (final summary) and deliverable line 125 (Section IV) state "33 numbered findings (15 HIGH / 10 MEDIUM / 8 LOW)", while the report's own findings sections enumerate 44 numbered entries (TL-1–9, RCF-1–5, EX-1–4, ES-1–3, SHA-1–5, MIP-1–6, OC-1–9, OP-1–3), 26 of them HIGH-rated counting split ratings at the higher level. The distribution appears nowhere in the rollout before the final summary — it was asserted, never tallied, then repeated to the user.
- base1.md:5485 / deliverable line 26: executive summary Item 2 cross-refers "(see Items 7, 8, 9 below)" for the Officer's Certificate §4(g)/(h)/(n) contradictions, but those contradictions are Items 5, 6 and 9 (liquidity, ES net cash proceeds, intercompany); Items 7 and 8 are governance and MIP.
- base1.md:2666 / deliverable line 161: while reading the RCF credit agreement the run extracted the provision as "Section 11.04 — Relationship to Other Restructuring Documents", then cited it as "Section 11.03" in finding RCF-5(b); §11.03 is Amendments and Waivers (source headings confirm). The report itself flags the identical error type in the Exchange Agreement (EX-3, deliverable line 169) — so the gap is expert practice (a final cite-check), not analytic ability.
- base1.md:5500–5502: after generating the docx the run "round-trip extracted to confirm content integrity" — a format check, not a content check; and both context compactions (base1.md:2194, base1.md:4654) meant final numbers were drafted from reconstructed summaries, which only a recount against the finished artifact catches.

2. EDIT systemprompt.md (+3 lines at end) — the trigger line required for the skill to load: "Before finalizing any review deliverable (gap report, issue list, closing checklist summary), load the `cite-check` skill and run it on the finished text before generating the output file." Directory name appears verbatim, in the same edit, per validation rule 1; kept to two lines of always-on cost.

KEEP_BASE for guardrails.md, LongTermMEMORY.md, tool_guidance.md, scripts/, sub_agents/, plugin/ — no trajectory evidence for further practitioner-knowledge changes. The run's substantive findings (94.34% participation vs 95% condition, NCP ≈ $52.7M vs $55M floor, board inversion, MIP 9.5%/60-40/3-yr, missing 2L Indenture and A&R Intercreditor) verified accurate against the sources and are not re-fixed. Tool/infra failures (podman unavailable, /tmp write permissions) are procedure, owned by the parallel candidate.

stages.label: agg1
stages.notes:
kept -> scripts/extract_all_docs.py (inv1) -> podman traceback wall hit in 2/2 rollouts lacking the script (base1 ln 37-63, dom1 ln 33-48), each burning a read_doc.py source read to discover `--in host`; with the script, 9/9 docs extracted on first call with line-count inventory (inv1 ln 31-41)
kept -> tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md (inv1) -> final-output podman failure recovered in 1 step citing the guidance (inv1 ln 5241-5244); dom1, lacking it, re-read read_doc.py's 107 lines to clear the same failure
kept -> guardrails.md (inv1) -> agent persisted findings to .scratch/findings.md immediately after compaction summaries (inv1 ln 2168-2170, refreshed ln 5115) across 3 compactions; base1's 2 compactions (ln 2194-2270, 4654-4779) preserved no intermediate state
kept -> LongTermMEMORY.md (inv1) -> baseline economics held consistent across inv1's 337-line report with stated counts matching enumeration (42 findings; 8 Critical / 14 High); replaces empty base file
kept -> skills/cite-check/SKILL.md + systemprompt trigger (dom1) -> all 3 targeted defect classes verified in base1's deliverable: stated 15/10/8=33 findings vs 44 enumerated entries (deliverable ln 125); exec-summary cross-ref "Items 7, 8, 9" should be 5, 6, 9 (ln 26); RCF-5(b) cites Section 11.03 for the clause that is 11.04 (ln 161, confirmed vs source docx); dom1's own rollout cite-check pass caught/fixed analogous errors (firm name, segment name, Part 13->14 cross-ref) and final verify confirmed 40 rows = 6/16/13/5 consistent

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: a review deliverable that states facts about itself — finding counts, severity tallies, internal cross-references, section citations — drafted across a long session with multiple compactions, where final numbers and citations get written from reconstructed summaries rather than the record
experience.lesson: before the deliverable file is generated, run a named final-pass skill (e.g. skills/cite-check/SKILL.md) wired to fire by a systemprompt.md trigger: recount every stated tally from the artifact's own enumeration under a stated counting convention, resolve every internal cross-reference, re-verify every citation and quotation against the extracted source text, and re-run after any fix. A format/validation check on the generated file does not catch this class
experience.evidence: the cite-check row and its confounded trigger row. base1 extracted the correct section heading mid-read yet cited §11.03 for the §11.04 conflict clause in the shipped report, with mismatched counts and cross-references surviving a format-only final check; dom1's pass caught nine such errors pre-delivery and agg1's recounted and verified cleanly — the error class is write-time, not read-time, which is why the extraction and memory edits did not prevent it
experience.confidence: medium — the read-time/write-time contrast and dom1's nine caught errors are strong, but inv1 shipped a self-consistent report without the skill, and adoption was a trivial single-candidate pool that establishes nothing

+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/banking-finance__compare-closing-documents-against-restructuring-conditions/harnesses/inv1/scripts/extract_all_docs.py	2026-10-25 12:20:28
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Extract every task document to plain text, with a sanity gate on each output.
+
+Drives the runtime-provided scripts/read_doc.py in --in host mode (its sandbox
+default fails in this environment: no podman) for each binary document under
+documents/, writes .scratch/<name>.txt, and fails loudly per file if extraction
+errors, returns a Python traceback, or produces a near-empty file — so a parser
+error can never be mistaken for document text.
+
+Usage:
+    python3 scripts/extract_all_docs.py [source_dir] [dest_dir]
+
+Defaults: documents/ -> .scratch/. On success prints one inventory line per file
+(path + line count, to plan reading order) and exits 0. On failure prints a FAIL
+line with the reason for each bad file and exits 1 — read the reason and fix the
+cause; do not re-run blindly.
+"""
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+MIN_LINES = 20  # real extractions here run 150+ lines; captured tracebacks are ~18
+BAD_MARKERS = ("Traceback (most recent call last)",)
+
+
+def find_read_doc() -> Path:
+    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+    for cand in (here / "read_doc.py", Path.cwd() / "scripts" / "read_doc.py"):
+        if cand.is_file():
+            return cand
+    sys.stderr.write(
+        "runtime did not provide scripts/read_doc.py; "
+        "fall back to reading each document with the read tool\n"
+    )
+    sys.exit(2)
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    src = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("documents")
+    dst = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else Path(".scratch")
+    reader = find_read_doc()
+
+    if not src.is_dir():
+        sys.stderr.write(f"source directory not found: {src}\n")
+        return 1
+    files = sorted(
+        p for p in src.iterdir()
+        if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower().lstrip(".") in ("docx", "pdf", "pptx", "xlsx")
+    )
+    if not files:
+        sys.stderr.write(f"no binary documents found in {src}\n")
+        return 1
+
+    dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    failures = []
+    for f in files:
+        try:
+            proc = subprocess.run(
+                [sys.executable, str(reader), str(f), "--in", "host"],
+                capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
+                errors="replace", timeout=300,
+            )
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            failures.append(f.name)
+            print(f"FAIL {f.name}: extraction timed out")
+            continue
+        text = proc.stdout or ""
+        nlines = len([ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()])
+        if proc.returncode != 0:
+            reason = (proc.stderr or "extraction failed").strip().splitlines()[-1]
+        elif nlines < MIN_LINES:
+            reason = f"only {nlines} lines extracted"
+        elif any(m in text for m in BAD_MARKERS):
+            reason = "output contains a Python traceback, not document text"
+        else:
+            reason = None
+        if reason:
+            failures.append(f.name)

+---
+name: cite-check
+description: Final pre-delivery verification pass for a legal review deliverable — reconcile stated counts to the enumerated findings, resolve internal cross-references, and re-verify every citation against the cited source document.
+---
+
+# Cite-check the finished deliverable
+
+A practitioner never sends a review work product to the client without one
+final pass over the assembled text. The analysis is done at that point; this
+pass checks the artifact against itself and against the record. Run it on the
+complete deliverable text immediately before generating the output file, and
+again after any later edit.
+
+## Three checks, in order
+
+1. COUNTS. Every number the report states about itself must be recounted from
+   the artifact's own enumeration — never from memory, a draft tally, or a
+   summary written before the findings were final.
+   - List the enumerated findings from the finished text (IDs and severity
+     ratings as printed) and count them.
+   - State the counting convention and apply it consistently: each numbered
+     entry counts once; a split rating (e.g. MEDIUM/HIGH) counts at its
+     higher level; entries marked "no finding" are counted or excluded —
+     say which.
+   - Confirm every stated distribution (by severity, by document, and every
+     total in the executive summary, body and closing message) reconciles to
+     that count. Fix the text, not the tally.
+
+2. CROSS-REFERENCES. Every internal pointer must resolve on the reader's side.
+   - For each "see Item N", "see Section N below", "see Finding X-N": turn to
+     the pointed-to item and confirm it actually bears the point being made.
+     Adjacent item numbers are the common error, especially after renumbering
+     or after working from a summary of an earlier draft.
+   - Each executive-summary item must map to the same finding as the detail
+     section: same facts, same severity, same recommended action.
+
+3. CITATIONS. Every cite is re-verified against the cited document
+   immediately before delivery — not as a memory of the first read.
+   - For each section or Article citation: open the cited document at that
+     section and confirm the heading and substance match the proposition.
+     Neighbouring section numbers (11.03 vs 11.04) are the common drift.
+   - For each quotation: confirm the quoted words appear verbatim in the
+     source.
+   - Cite each document by the name it bears in the matter set, not a
+     shorthand the reader cannot resolve.
+
+If any check fails, fix the deliverable text and re-run all three — one fix
+can move a count or a number.
+

+

+all three failure modes: a summary stating "15 HIGH / 10 MEDIUM / 8 LOW" (33

+itself flagged the same error type in one of the closing documents it
+reviewed. The run verified the generated file's format but never compared the

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Extract every task document to plain text, with a sanity gate on each output.
+
+Drives the runtime-provided scripts/read_doc.py in --in host mode (its sandbox
+default fails in this environment: no podman) for each binary document under
+documents/, writes .scratch/<name>.txt, and fails loudly per file if extraction
+errors, returns a Python traceback, or produces a near-empty file — so a parser
+error can never be mistaken for document text.
+
+Usage:
+    python3 scripts/extract_all_docs.py [source_dir] [dest_dir]
+
+Defaults: documents/ -> .scratch/. On success prints one inventory line per file
+(path + line count, to plan reading order) and exits 0. On failure prints a FAIL
+line with the reason for each bad file and exits 1 — read the reason and fix the
+cause; do not re-run blindly.
+"""
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+MIN_LINES = 20  # real extractions here run 150+ lines; captured tracebacks are ~18
+BAD_MARKERS = ("Traceback (most recent call last)",)
+
+
+def find_read_doc() -> Path:
+    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+    for cand in (here / "read_doc.py", Path.cwd() / "scripts" / "read_doc.py"):
+        if cand.is_file():
+            return cand
+    sys.stderr.write(
+        "runtime did not provide scripts/read_doc.py; "
+        "fall back to reading each document with the read tool\n"
+    )
+    sys.exit(2)
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    src = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("documents")
+    dst = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else Path(".scratch")
+    reader = find_read_doc()
+
+    if not src.is_dir():
+        sys.stderr.write(f"source directory not found: {src}\n")
+        return 1
+    files = sorted(
+        p for p in src.iterdir()
+        if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower().lstrip(".") in ("docx", "pdf", "pptx", "xlsx")
+    )
+    if not files:
+        sys.stderr.write(f"no binary documents found in {src}\n")
+        return 1
+
+    dst.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    failures = []
+    for f in files:
+        try:
+            proc = subprocess.run(
+                [sys.executable, str(reader), str(f), "--in", "host"],
+                capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
+                errors="replace", timeout=300,
+            )
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            failures.append(f.name)
+            print(f"FAIL {f.name}: extraction timed out")
+            continue
+        text = proc.stdout or ""
+        nlines = len([ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()])
+        if proc.returncode != 0:
+            reason = (proc.stderr or "extraction failed").strip().splitlines()[-1]
+        elif nlines < MIN_LINES:
+            reason = f"only {nlines} lines extracted"
+        elif any(m in text for m in BAD_MARKERS):
+            reason = "output contains a Python traceback, not document text"
+        else:
+            reason = None
+        if reason:
+            failures.append(f.name)
+            print(f"FAIL {f.name}: {reason}")
+            continue
+        (dst / (f.stem + ".txt")).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
+        print(f"OK   {dst/(f.stem + '.txt')}  ({nlines} lines)")
+
+    print(f"--- {len(files) - len(failures)}/{len(files)} extracted to {dst}/")
+    if failures:
+        print("files marked FAIL were NOT written; fix the cause before proceeding")
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
